GCTS research notebook · 6 November 2026 UTC

Lifted equality search for Wang proofs

The prover can substitute an equality even when its clause still contains alternatives. The learned scheduler proved all nine positive held-out requests. An independent checker replayed each proof from the original statement.

SearchFailure markingsControlsWang squaresRead the proofs

Carry the alternatives through a rewrite

Select a term addressIndex an equation by the outer symbol of the term it can rewrite. Unify it with a subterm in another clause, with separately scoped variables and checked sorts.
Keep the residual clausesReplace the chosen occurrence and retain the unused literals of both parents. Equality resolution can remove a disequality whose two sides unify.
Check the winning pathSpecialize the found derivation and expand each equality move into ground instances and ordinary resolution. The existing translation-only Wang palette checks those records.

For the incidence example, a named point lies on one line, and that line equals one of two named lines. The conclusion is a disjunction of two incidence statements. The input contains only typed symbols and formulas.

The rewrite arm indexes nonvariable terms in different clauses and orients equations by schematic size and syntax. These are search restrictions. The experiment establishes sound proofs through the existing checker and measures success within fixed work bounds.

Equality rewriting within clauses is an established theorem-proving technique. The experiment tests an encoding of those moves into the fixed Wang checker and measures the effect of reusable failure markings and clause priority. Bachmair and Ganzinger on resolution and superposition

Learn where a rewrite cannot fit

The indexed outer symbols already agree. Each learned mark points further into the terms. A rigid clash compares two different function or constant symbols. An alias clash points to two occurrences of one variable that would have to match different rigid symbols.

On the held-out set, the two frozen marks skipped 89 rewrite unifications. The matched marked and unmarked searches stored identical clauses and found identical proofs with the same priority setting.

Compare the search arms

The ground unit arm uses the existing equality tactic with proposed terms for addition. The lifted axioms arm searches with explicit equality clauses. Plain and learned rewriting use the same indexed moves and search limits as each other. Each lifted arm has a limit of 12,000 offers or 3,000 stored clauses.

The scheduler is a one-decision epsilon-greedy policy. It chooses how much to favor unit clauses descended from the negated goal. Training observes only the chosen arm's outcome. Success earns more reward when it takes fewer offers. Bounded failures earn a penalty. The frozen policy chose a bias of 24.
